newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - NZ$ comment not on current conditions - Brash.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - NZ$ comment not on current conditions - Brash.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand governor Don Brash said on Friday that comments he made about the New Zealand dollar being overvalued at a private dinner on Thursday night were not related to current monetary conditions.

"It was not about monetary conditions at all," Brash told Reuters before a private lunch at the Centre for Independent Studies in Sydney. He said he had responded to a question about the New Zealand economy and the New Zealand dollar but that his comments were the same has he had been making in recent months.
Comments attributed to Brash contributed to a fall in the New Zealand dollar in trading on Friday.
Earlier this month, Brash said the bank would prefer a different mix of monetary conditions, with a lower exchange rate and higher interest rates.
Brash told Reuters he would not repeat his Thursday night comments and he would not comment current monetary conditions or the inflation outlook.
He said a regular Reserve Bank statement on the economy was due out in less than two weeks and the bank would make its comments then. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
